attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04). Installed aide/aide-common, added a custom rule (/etc/aide/aide.conf.d/99_aide_etc_baseline) applying the full content-hash (Full = InodeData+StaticFile+Checksums) selector recursively to /etc (excluding /etc/mtab, a proc symlink), since the stock Ubuntu config only tracked /etc metadata plus a handful of specific files. Generated the baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db, verified it detects both a modified existing /etc file and a newly created /etc file, reverted the test changes, and regenerated a clean baseline reflecting the true starting state. The distro's dailyaidecheck.timer is enabled/active for ongoing automated checks. Completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and aide.db/config checksums, issued `systemctl reboot` via a detached background wrapper so the exec call returned before disconnect, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and confirmed the AIDE database/config checksums were byte-identical post-reboot and that a fresh /etc-scoped check post-reboot showed zero differences under /etc (all changes were expected /run tmpfs and /var/log/dmesg.0 churn, none in /etc).
